board: Arkansas State Board of Public Accountancy

cycle.note: Arkansas licenses renew every year; CPE is due December 31: either 40 hours this year or 120 over the last three years. 4 ethics hours (1 on Arkansas laws and rules) every three years.

requirements.label: Annual CPE
requirements.note: 40 hours this calendar year — or 120 over the last three (17 CAR 236-1203).

requirements.label: Accounting, ethics, attest or tax
requirements.note: 20% of your hours (40% if you're in public practice) in accounting, ethics, attest or tax.

requirements.label: Attest & accounting theory
requirements.note: If you do attest or compilation work: another 20% in attest and accounting theory.

requirements.label: Group learning
requirements.note: Self-study, nano and publications together can't exceed 80%, so at least 8 hours must be group (live or webinar).

requirements.label: Nano-learning
requirements.note: Maximum, not a target. No more than 4 nano-learning hours a year.

requirements.label: Personal development
requirements.note: Personal development topics don't count toward Arkansas CPE.

requirements.label: Ethics
requirements.note: 4 hours of ethics every 36 months, including 1 hour on Arkansas Board laws and rules (the Board's free "Arkansas Board Laws and Rules" course counts).

requirements.label: Arkansas laws & rules
requirements.note: 1 hour on Arkansas Board laws and rules every 36 months. We count courses with "Arkansas" and "laws", "rules" or "ethics" in the title.

newLicensee.note: The year you're first licensed is prorated by month (about 3⅓ hours a month). Ethics starts with your first full calendar year.

licenseDateHint: Arkansas licenses renew every year; CPE is due December 31.
issueDateHint: If you were first licensed this year, this year's hours are prorated by month.
limitsNotTracked: Subject and group percentages scale with the 120-hour option (48/24 and 24); the app checks this year's 40.
recordRetention: Keep CPE records for five years after the end of the year completed.
toVerify: New-licensee proration (3⅓ hours a month is from a third-party source).
Whether the 36-month window is rolling (the rule) or fixed (the Board's summary).
